title: 202 Accepted for moving and deleting teams
summary: Stack #101 → #102 → #103: the public API learns to answer 202, a kit stores the operation in Redis and a job replays it with the same synchronous verb.

related.label: #101 · accepted_verbs engine
related.note: Base of the stack: the platform learns to answer 202.

related.label: #102 · AsyncOperations kit
related.note: State in Redis, lock and actor.

related.label: Stack review (v3)
related.note: 19 findings, 21 verified, and an English explainer.

nodes.label: Integrator
nodes.subtitle: x-api-key or OAuth
nodes.summary: Whoever calls the public API. It used to get a 200 saying "done" about something that wasn't; now it gets a 202 with an identifier and polls for how it ended.

nodes.label: 202 engine
nodes.subtitle: PR #101
nodes.summary: Teaches the platform to answer 202 when an RPC verb declares it. Nothing uses it in this PR: the generated OpenAPI comes out identical, which is its safety argument.

nodes.label: ResourcesController
nodes.subtitle: public_api
nodes.summary: The public API's generic controller. The success code was hardwired: create 201, everything else 200.

nodes.label: #rpc
nodes.subtitle: POST …/:resource/:verb
nodes.summary: Runs the repository's RPC verb and renders the entity. The status now comes from rpc_status instead of always being 200.

nodes.label: #rpc_status
nodes.subtitle: → :accepted | :ok
nodes.summary: Asks the resource's rest capability whether the verb is in accepted_verbs. The decision lives in the .yml, not here, so no existing endpoint changes.

nodes.label: #index · #show
nodes.subtitle: GET …/operations
nodes.summary: The usual read path, untouched. It's how the client polls for the result of an accepted operation.

nodes.label: rest capability
nodes.subtitle: resource_catalog
nodes.summary: The .yml block that exposes a resource over REST. It gains the accepted_verbs list.

nodes.label: #accepted_verb?
nodes.summary: The only question the rest of the engine asks the resource: does this verb answer 202?

nodes.label: Rest::Resource
nodes.subtitle: resource_catalog
nodes.summary: A resource's REST view, built when the application boots.

nodes.label: #validate_accepted_verbs!
nodes.subtitle: fails at boot
nodes.summary: At boot, rejects a CRUD verb (already published as 200/201 in frozen versions), a verb the resource doesn't implement, and one that returns a collection. An error here breaks boot in CI; it never reaches production as a 500.

nodes.label: OpenAPI generator
nodes.subtitle: lib/oas · public_api/oas
nodes.summary: The part that documents the 202 in the OpenAPI and the part that reads it back in the contract specs.

nodes.label: Rpc#response_class
nodes.summary: Picks Response::Accepted when the verb is marked as accepted.

nodes.label: Response::Accepted
nodes.subtitle: 202 / ACCEPTED
nodes.summary: The 202 response as it appears in the OpenAPI.

nodes.label: Operation#successful_response
nodes.summary: It used to assume a 200 or a 201 and blew up with a meaningless NoMethodError. Now it looks for the first of 200/201/202 and, if there is none, says which ones are documented.

nodes.label: AsyncOperations kit
nodes.subtitle: public_api/async_operations
nodes.summary: Where an accepted operation lives, how two are kept from stepping on the same target, and how it remembers who requested it. It started in backend/lib, with no owner; it moved to the component that owns the 202.

notes.text: Resolved in the second round: the kit no longer lives in backend/lib (an unowned area in CODEOWNERS) but in components/public_api.

nodes.label: State
nodes.subtitle: TTL 24 h
nodes.summary: An operation's lifecycle in Redis: pending → processing → completed | failed.

nodes.label: #create!
nodes.subtitle: SET … EX 86400
nodes.summary: Writes the record as pending and sets the 24-hour TTL. It's the only write that sets a TTL.

nodes.label: #processing!
nodes.summary: Marks the operation as in progress and records started_at, which is now exposed to the client.

nodes.label: #completed! · #failed!
nodes.summary: Closes the operation with its result or its reason, plus finished_at.

nodes.label: #transition!
nodes.subtitle: SET XX KEEPTTL
nodes.summary: Every transition goes through here. KEEPTTL keeps the 24 h window from stretching with each change; XX prevents resurrecting an operation that expired between the read and the write.

notes.text: Validated over HTTP: the TTL measured before and after completed holds. SET XX KEEPTTL requires Redis ≥ 6; every environment in the repository runs 7.0.

nodes.label: .get_many
nodes.subtitle: MGET
nodes.summary: Reads a batch of operations in a single round trip to Redis.

notes.text: Resolved: polling used to do one GET per id, up to 100 sequential round trips.

nodes.label: .parse
nodes.summary: Deserializes a record and treats one it can't read as missing, instead of taking down the whole batch with a 500. This matters because for 24 h records written by two revisions of the code coexist.

nodes.label: InFlightGuard
nodes.subtitle: TTL 15 min
nodes.summary: Only one in-flight operation per target. The second one gets a 409.

nodes.label: #acquire
nodes.subtitle: SET NX EX 900
nodes.summary: Takes the lock only if it doesn't exist. Returns false if another operation holds it, and the repository turns that into a 409 Conflict.

nodes.label: #renew
nodes.summary: Restarts the lock window when the job starts, instead of counting it from acceptance.

notes.text: Resolves the most serious finding of the first round: the lock expired after 15 minutes while the work was still queued or running, and a second operation on the same team was accepted.

nodes.label: #release
nodes.subtitle: compare-and-delete
nodes.summary: Releases the lock only if it's still ours, using WATCH/MULTI on the connection that yields WATCH. Lua wasn't used because MockRedis implements eval as a no-op and the specs would have passed without testing anything.

nodes.label: Actor
nodes.summary: A snapshot of who requested the operation, to replay it with the same permissions.

nodes.label: .serialize
nodes.summary: Stores the type and id of the permission context (Access or Company) and the OAuth and api key contexts. It never stores tokens or permissions: only identities.

nodes.label: .deserialize
nodes.subtitle: becomer_id: nil
nodes.summary: Rebuilds the context by looking up the record by id, so a deleted account makes the operation fail instead of running with zombie permissions. Permissions are reread from the database.

notes.text: OAuth scopes are not revalidated: their check is a controller before_action and the job doesn't go through it. A token revoked between acceptance and replay doesn't stop it.

links.note: The check the replay doesn't repeat.

nodes.label: Record · Status
nodes.summary: What gets stored: what was requested, by whom, how it ended, and the four possible states.

nodes.label: Existing gates
nodes.subtitle: unchanged
nodes.summary: Three pieces the stack doesn't touch but its safety depends on.

nodes.label: PolicyHook
nodes.subtitle: repository hook
nodes.summary: It hangs off the repository, not the controller. That's why the job also goes through it and verb permissions are checked again on replay.

nodes.label: EndpointChecker
nodes.summary: Decides whether an endpoint exists in the version the client requests. Turns version_changes into a 404 on stable versions.

nodes.label: validate_api_scopes
nodes.subtitle: before_action
nodes.summary: The only OAuth scope validation, and it's a controller filter: the replay doesn't go through here.

links.note: Where the actor is rehydrated without revalidating the token.

nodes.label: teams.operation resource
nodes.subtitle: PR #103
nodes.summary: The file that is the API: verbs, permissions, scopes, response schema, and which versions each thing exists in.

nodes.label: operation.yml
nodes.summary: Declares read and the three RPC verbs. The descriptions are the contract the client sees in the portal.

nodes.label: accepted_verbs
nodes.subtitle: move · delete · delete_membership
nodes.summary: The three RPC verbs that answer 202. read isn't there and couldn't be: the boot validation would reject it.

nodes.label: endpoint_added ×5
nodes.subtitle: under '2026-07-01'
nodes.summary: Registered after the last stable version: the resulting range is 2026-07-02..∞, so they exist from the 2026-10-01 beta onward and answer 404 on the four stable ones. Validated over HTTP.

nodes.label: dev_teams_async_operations
nodes.summary: The per-company switch. Without it, the four verbs answer 403 even if the client requests the beta.

nodes.label: Repositories::Operations
nodes.subtitle: mutates nothing
nodes.summary: Quickly decides whether the request deserves a 202 and records it. Nothing is mutated here.

nodes.label: #move_team
nodes.summary: Validates the cheap things (the team exists, the destination exists and is manageable, the flags are on) and delegates to #accept. The expensive parts (the 4-level cap, the hierarchy) are deferred to the replay.

nodes.label: #delete_team
nodes.summary: Same as the move, with no destination to resolve.

nodes.label: #delete_membership
nodes.summary: Accepts deleting a membership. It now takes the lock of the team it belongs to, not the row's.

notes.text: Resolved: delete_team and delete_membership on the same team used to be accepted at once because the lock was per row. Validated over HTTP: it now returns 409 both ways.

nodes.label: #accept
nodes.summary: Actor snapshot, lock, Redis record and enqueue. If the record or the enqueue fails, it releases the lock before propagating the error, so the team isn't left locked for a quarter of an hour.

nodes.label: #operations_gate
nodes.summary: The two feature gates: async operations and nested teams.

notes.text: Validated over HTTP: each disabled flag gives its own, correct message. But no test asserts the text and none runs with dev_nested_teams off: swapping them wouldn't break the suite.

nodes.label: #read
nodes.subtitle: 1..100 ids
nodes.summary: The poll. It bounds and deduplicates before touching Redis and resolves the company from the permission context, never from the client.

nodes.label: #entity_from_record
nodes.summary: Turns the record into the public entity, including started_at and expires_at.

nodes.label: RunOperationJob
nodes.subtitle: retry: 0
nodes.summary: Replays the mutation by calling the same method on the same repository as the synchronous endpoint. No retries: a failure is reported to the client, not repeated blindly.

links.label: Review findings
links.note: The lock and the false failed were addressed in the first round.

nodes.label: #perform
nodes.summary: Reads the record (if it's gone, it mutates nothing), marks processing, renews the lock, replays and reports. Only the replay goes inside the rescue.

nodes.label: #replay
nodes.summary: Rehydrates the actor, validates the stored input (it travels as JSON and another revision may have written it) and dispatches to the matching synchronous verb.

nodes.label: #move_team
nodes.summary: Builds a Dtos::Team::Move with the stored id and destination and calls Repositories::Teams#move.

notes.text: It never passes source_parent_team_id, so it forces the source parent to be inferred from the people groups graph, which refreshes asynchronously. With Sidekiq draining a backlog, the move failed twice with invalid_parent_team; the same move with an explicit parent worked.

links.note: The synchronous verb it delegates to; source_parent_team_id is missing there.

nodes.label: #report
nodes.summary: Writes completed or failed and logs the result.

notes.text: Resolved: it used to live inside the replay's rescue, and a log call failing after an applied mutation rewrote it as failed. The client retried something already done.

nodes.label: #team_result
nodes.summary: What the job stores as the result of a move: team_id, parent_team_id and depth.

notes.text: Validated over HTTP: parent_team_id and depth come out null in 100% of completed moves, even though the database has a parent and depth. The .yml documents them as part of the result.

links.note: This is where the nulls come from: it reads caches that only #read fills.

nodes.label: #release_guard
nodes.subtitle: ensure
nodes.summary: Releases the lock no matter what. A worker that dies hard (OOM, SIGKILL) never gets here: the lock expires on its own.

nodes.label: Synchronous verbs
nodes.subtitle: the existing ones
nodes.summary: The repositories the replay calls again. They only change because of the refactor.

nodes.label: Repositories::Teams
nodes.summary: Moves and deletes teams. It now uses the two extracted concerns.

nodes.label: #move
nodes.subtitle: line 162
nodes.summary: The actual move: resolves source and destination with ParentResolution and calls Interactors::MoveTeam.

nodes.label: #delete
nodes.subtitle: line 136
nodes.summary: The actual delete, with Interactors::DeleteTeam.

nodes.label: #entity_from_active_record
nodes.subtitle: line 385
nodes.summary: Builds the Team entity. It reads depth and parent_team_id from two caches that only #read populates; on any other path, #move included, they are nil.

links.note: What stores that result as if it were the final position.

nodes.label: Repositories::Memberships
nodes.summary: Deletes memberships, direct or inherited.

nodes.label: #delete
nodes.subtitle: line 371
nodes.summary: Deleting an inherited membership removes the employee from the subteams it comes from, and requires permission on each one.

nodes.label: Shared refactor
nodes.summary: Two copies that weren't identical, and the part that was actually extracted. Each repository keeps its own wrapper with its cache and its failure policy.

nodes.label: Concerns::NestedTeamsFlag
nodes.summary: The nested teams flag read.

notes.text: This read bypasses the feature cache: it materializes the whole catalog (~700 flags) to check one. During polling it's paid on every call.

nodes.label: Concerns::ParentResolution
nodes.summary: Resolves the parent team the DTO carries and checks manage permission on it.

nodes.label: Redis
nodes.subtitle: $redis · persistent
nodes.summary: The backend instance, deliberately separate from the evictable cache. It gains a new namespace. It shares the instance with the Sidekiq queues.

nodes.label: Operation record
nodes.subtitle: …:{co}:teams.operation:{uuid}
nodes.summary: A 400-600 byte JSON per operation, with a 24-hour TTL. After that, polling returns 404, indistinguishable from an id that never existed.

nodes.label: In-flight lock
nodes.subtitle: …:inflight:{co}:teams.team:{id}
nodes.summary: One key per team holding the id of the operation that has it.

nodes.label: Sidekiq
nodes.subtitle: within_30_seconds queue
nodes.summary: The background job system. The SLO the job declares picks the queue, and the one picked is the low-latency queue for work that can take minutes.

nodes.label: Interactors::MoveTeam
nodes.summary: Moves the team with the 4-level cap and the hierarchy checks. The replay reaches it through the same path as the synchronous endpoint.

nodes.label: Interactors::DeleteTeam
nodes.summary: Detaches the team from its parent, deletes its people groups and ends its memberships, in one transaction.

nodes.label: people_groups_v2
nodes.subtitle: closure table
nodes.summary: The hierarchy table. Changing a reference deletes and reinserts every edge of the group and its dependents.

notes.text: The people_groups_v2:edges:<company_id> lock spans the whole tenant and has no wait timeout. Getting it off the HTTP thread is the underlying reason for the whole stack.

nodes.label: RefreshGroupJob
nodes.summary: Re-propagates inherited memberships upward, up to 5 levels, with two Kafka messages per employee and level. It keeps running after completed.

nodes.label: Webhooks teams/team/*
nodes.summary: The existing webhooks. Since the replay calls the real repository, they fire with the real entity.

edges.label: POST operations/move_team
edges.summary: The client asks to move a team in the beta version.

edges.label: 202 · id, pending
edges.summary: The change in one arrow: the API stops claiming the work is done and returns an identifier the client can poll.
edges.data: { id: uuid, status: pending, kind, target_id, accepted_at, expires_at }

edges.summary: The controller decides the success code.

edges.label: declares
edges.summary: The resource's .yml feeds the list the controller checks.

edges.label: validates at boot
edges.summary: Three guardrails that run when the resource registry is built.

edges.label: 404 on stable
edges.summary: The version range comes from the version_changes registry.

edges.label: Manage on the target
edges.summary: The hook checks that the caller can manage the team before entering the verb.

edges.label: snapshot of the caller
edges.data: { type: access | company, id, oauth, api_key }

edges.label: 409 if one exists
edges.summary: If the lock is already taken, the verb returns Outcome.invalid_state and the client gets a 409.

edges.label: TTL 24 h
edges.data: Record as JSON: operation_id, company_id, kind, target_id, status, actor, input

edges.label: SET XX KEEPTTL
edges.summary: No transition stretches the window or resurrects an expired operation.

edges.label: only this goes in the rescue
the same synchronous verb
edges.summary: The decision that removes the most risk: the job reimplements nothing; it calls the method the existing endpoint calls. That's why permissions are revalidated and the webhooks fire on their own.

edges.label: company-wide lock
edges.summary: Rebuilds the closure table under an advisory lock that spans the whole tenant.

edges.label: on reads too
edges.summary: Reads go through the same gate as writes: turning the flag off as a kill switch leaves the client unable to poll operations already accepted.

flows.title: Accept
flows.summary: Inside the HTTP request: decide and record, nothing more.

messages.label: permission, flags, destination
messages.note: If a gate fails, it ends here: 403 or 400 and nothing is enqueued.

messages.label: 202 · id, pending
messages.note: Two Redis commands and one enqueue. The request doesn't wait for the work.

flows.title: Replay
flows.summary: The job repeats the synchronous call; everything expensive happens here.

messages.label: get · processing!
messages.note: If the record is gone, it mutates nothing.

messages.label: renew
messages.note: The lock window is counted from here, not from acceptance.

messages.label: company-wide lock
messages.note: No wait timeout: this is what moves off the HTTP thread.

flows.title: Poll
flows.summary: The endpoint the client calls in a loop.

tour.title: How the 202 works
tour.summary: Ten steps from concept to method. Each one opens only what's needed.

steps.title: The verb can now answer 202
steps.body_html:
Everything used to be 200, which means "done". Now an RPC verb can declare that it has only accepted the work.

The engine lives in the platform and nothing uses it in its own PR: the first consumer is teams.operation.

steps.title: Three guardrails at boot
steps.body_html:
What happens: when the resource registry is built, #validate_accepted_verbs! rejects a CRUD verb, a nonexistent one and one that returns a collection.

Why it matters: an error here breaks boot in CI; it never reaches production as a 500.

steps.title: Beta only, and only with the flag
steps.body_html:
What travels: the version the client requests, checked against the 2026-07-02..∞ range that comes from endpoint_added.

Outside the beta, 404. Inside it, without dev_teams_async_operations, 403. Both validated over HTTP.

steps.title: Accepting is deciding and recording
steps.body_html:
Inside the request only two Redis commands and one enqueue happen. The expensive work doesn't happen here.

What triggers it: Operations#accept, which also releases the lock if the record or the enqueue fails.

steps.title: One lock per team, now renewed
steps.body_html:
What travels: a …:inflight:{co}:teams.team:{id} key holding the operation id, with a 15-minute lifetime.

The second round added #renew: the window restarts when the job starts, so a slow job sitting in the queue no longer lets a second operation on the same team through.

steps.title: The job repeats the synchronous verb
steps.body_html:
Nothing is reimplemented: RunOperationJob#move_team calls Repositories::Teams#move, the existing one. That's why verb permissions are revalidated and the webhooks fire on their own.

Watch out: it doesn't pass source_parent_team_id. Under load the move failed twice with invalid_parent_team.

steps.title: The lock moves off the HTTP thread
steps.body_html:
Rebuilding the hierarchy takes a lock that spans the whole company and has no wait timeout. That no longer happens inside the request.

And completed doesn't mean "fully propagated": the cascade of inherited memberships continues afterwards.

steps.title: The result doesn't include the position
steps.body_html:
What travels: { team_id, parent_team_id, depth }. The last two always come out null: #entity_from_active_record reads them from caches that only #read fills.

The .yml promises them. Confirmed over HTTP in 100% of cases.

steps.title: Polling, in a single round trip
steps.body_html:
Before: one GET per id, up to 100 in sequence. Now a single MGET.

One thing remains: reads go through the same flag gate as writes. Turning the flag off leaves the client with no way to know how already-accepted work ended.

steps.title: What doesn't change
steps.body_html:
The teams domain and the platform gates don't have a single line of diff. Neither do the four stable OpenAPI specs.

Everything new lives in three lanes and is fenced in twice: beta version and flag.
